title: Sustained DPS reads a 6-loop window that has not always converged
body:
## Summary
sustainedCycle measures the period from the last two of 6 loops; for some chains the schedule is still in its transient and the reported sustained DPS is up to 4.2% high.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/combos/schedule.ts:140-155 takes `period = loopEnds[loops-1] - loopEnds[loops-2]` with cycles=6 (rankCombos passes 6 at schedule.ts:162; the builder at src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/combos/index.tsx:56 uses the default). A schedule with several competing cooldowns can need more than 6 loops to settle. Fixed: loop until the period is stable over two consecutive loop pairs (capped), then report the steady value.

## Flow
- build force-lightning, warcry, force-lightning, force-heal in the Combo builder
- sustainedCycle(chain, 6) -> 15.00 DPS; sustainedCycle(chain, 60) -> 14.40 DPS
- fix: iterate until the period repeats (cap ~64 loops), then report

## Expected impact
Designers ranking presets by sustained DPS get the steady figure; PRESET_DPS ranking could reorder. Risk: more loops at module load (6 presets, trivial).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - sustained DPS is the steady-state figure it claims to be
Before: 2 of 3000 seeded random chains (length 1-5 over the 14 COMBO_ABILITIES) differ >1% between cycles=6 and cycles=60 (max 4.2%: slam,force-lightning,death-field,warcry,force-lightning 22.42 vs 21.52)
After: predicted 0 of 3000 under a convergence loop
Method: probe - seeded random-chain vitest probe on the real schedule.ts (deleted after); the fix not built because the convergence rule is a modelling choice worth its own A/B
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/combos/schedule.ts:147 const period = loopEnds[loops - 1] - loopEnds[loops - 2];
probe: 3000 chains, 2 off: force-lightning,warcry,force-lightning,force-heal 6:15.00 7:15.00 60:14.40 | slam,force-lightning,death-field,warcry,force-lightning 6:22.42 7:22.42 60:21.52
instrument: the seeded 3000-chain probe (cycles=6 vs 60, >1% delta count) as a vitest; the fix must take it 2 -> 0 without moving any of the 6 PRESET_COMBOS figures by >1%

title: Three pipeline flows hand-roll one C++-reference disclosure; Heal's is weakest
body:
## Summary
DamagePipelineFlow, HealPipelineFlow and (since 770e272b) DirectHealthFlow each re-implement toggle state, the keyboard contract and the C++ panel; Heal's panel lacks the close button, region role, container-level Escape and focus return Damage has.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/damage-pipeline/DamagePipelineFlow.tsx:153-166,190-197,313-345 uses useId ids, a close button that returns focus, Escape on the container and role=region. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/damage-pipeline/HealPipelineFlow.tsx:11 uses a hard-coded id 'heal-pipeline-cpp-ref' (duplicate if mounted twice); :55-62 handles Escape only while the expanded node itself has focus; :91-103 has no close button, role or label. Fixed: one useCppRefDisclosure hook + CppRefPanel shared by all three flows.

## Flow
- Heal path: click 'Health += Heal', Tab away, press Escape -> panel stays open
- Damage path: same steps -> panel closes and focus returns to the node
- fix: extract hook + panel from DamagePipelineFlow, migrate Heal and Direct

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users get one dismiss contract across the three stacked flows; ~60 duplicated lines go. Risk: markup that DamagePipelineLegend.test.tsx reads.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one disclosure contract instead of three divergent copies
Before: dismiss affordances: Damage 3 (re-click, close button, Escape anywhere in the flow), Heal 2 (re-click, Escape on the focused node), Direct 2; 3 copies of the toggle+panel block
After: 3/3/3 affordances, 1 copy
Method: simulation - walked the three components' handlers; not built because it is a 3-file extraction (M) over tested markup
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: one parametrised RTL suite over all three flows: Escape after Tab closes, a close button exists and returns focus, the panel has role=region - red on Heal and Direct today

title: Hits tab presents invented per-weapon formulas as hit analysis
body:
## Summary
The Per-Weapon Hit Analysis shows Hit Rate, Hits/Swing and Trace Coverage computed from made-up constants, with no label saying they are heuristics.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/hits/HitsTab.tsx:26-36 derives hitRate = 70 + (1.5 - speed) * 20, hitsPerSwing by speed buckets and traceCoverage = 60 + avgDmg * 1.2; none comes from the UE trace system or a simulation. :75-80 normalises bars by hand (crit * 5, avgDmg / 40). Hit Detection Debug (HIT_STATS, TRACE_FRAMES) and the projectile planner are static demo data too. What fixed looks like is a product call: label as estimates, source from the combat simulator or UE trace telemetry, or remove.

## Flow
- Combat > Hits, pick 'Iron Longsword' -> Hit Rate 72%, Trace Coverage 73% shown as facts
- decide: label 'heuristic estimate' / wire to pof_combat_simulate / delete the panel

## Expected impact
Designers stop reading invented percentages as measured hit quality. Risk: removing a panel someone demos.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the hit panel says where its numbers come from
Before: 3 of 5 per-weapon stats are formula inventions with 0 source citations; 0 'estimate' labels
After: 0 unlabelled invented stats
Method: simulation - read the derivation; label vs source vs delete is a direction call no instrument decides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: operator decision: label / source from the combat simulator / remove

title: Hitstop timing bars use a hard-coded 1.5s scale and a fixed 10% offset
body:
## Summary
Hitstop Timing Configurations draws the anim bar at animDuration / 1.5 and the hitstop at a fixed left 10% with width (hitstop / MAX_HITSTOP) * 30%, so neither bar is to time scale.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/polish/FeedbackTab.tsx (Hitstop Timing block): width = animDuration / 1.5 - an ability over 1.5s overflows; the hitstop bar's class left-0 is overridden by style left '10%' and an arbitrary 30% scale, so Slam's 0.15s hitstop on a 1.2s anim draws as 30% of the track. HITSTOP_ABILITIES lives in src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/_shared/data-metrics.ts:284 (combat-metrics). Fixed: scale both bars by one max(animDuration) derived from the data.

## Flow
- Combat > Feedback, Hitstop Timing: Slam hitstop bar spans 30% of the track for 0.15s of 1.2s (true 12.5%)
- fix: derive maxDur from HITSTOP_ABILITIES; width = hitstop / maxDur

## Expected impact
The chart reads as time. Risk: low, visual only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - bars drawn to a time scale
Before: 5 of 5 hitstop bars mis-scaled (Slam 30% drawn vs 12.5% true; LightAttack1 6% vs 2.5%)
After: 5 of 5 to scale
Method: simulation - computed from the 5 HITSTOP_ABILITIES rows; placing the bar at the hit time needs a field the combat-metrics data lacks
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: RTL test reading each bar's width % against hitstop / max(animDuration); red on 5/5 today

title: Combo remove uses a post-filter cast index against the unfiltered chain
body:
## Summary
scheduleCombo drops unknown ability ids before numbering casts, but the builder removes by that index from the raw chain, so one unknown id makes every later remove delete the wrong block.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/combos/schedule.ts:96 filters ids missing from the table and :102 numbers casts by filtered position; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/combos/TimelineBlock.tsx:62 calls onRemove(cast.index) and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/combos/index.tsx:40-42 filters the raw chain by it. Unreachable from the UI today (chain ids come only from COMBO_ABILITIES and 6 PRESET_COMBOS, all known), but schedule.ts takes a swappable `abilities` table. Fixed: carry the raw chain position on ScheduledCast.

## Flow
- scheduleCombo(['melee1','ghost','slam']) -> casts numbered 0,1 (slam = 1)
- remove slam -> removeAbility(1) deletes 'ghost' instead

## Expected impact
Prevents a wrong-block delete once presets or ability tables come from UE sync. Risk: low.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - remove targets the block the user clicked
Before: 0 reachable cases today (0 unknown ids across 6 presets); 1 of 1 walked synthetic case deletes the wrong item
After: 0 of 1
Method: simulation - walked the index path; not built because no current input reaches it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test: schedule with an unknown id, assert each cast's raw chain position; red today

title: Damage flow placement is a hand-kept switch that silently drops new nodes
body:
## Summary
DamagePipelineFlow places nodes through a switch on node.id whose default returns null, so a step added to DAMAGE_PIPELINE renders nothing and no test notices.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/damage-pipeline/DamagePipelineFlow.tsx:229-245 maps DAMAGE_PIPELINE through `switch (node.id) { ... default: return null; }` plus a separate rows object (:173-184). The ground truth is DAMAGE_PIPELINE (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/damage-pipeline/pipeline-data.ts:5-17, 11 nodes); no test ties the drawn set to it. Fixed: a test derived from DAMAGE_PIPELINE (every id renders pipeline-node-<id>), ideally a position field on the data instead of the switch.

## Flow
- add a node to DAMAGE_PIPELINE
- the diagram still shows 11 nodes while its aria-label says 12 steps; every test stays green

## Expected impact
A future UE pipeline change cannot vanish from the diagram unnoticed. Risk: none for the test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - coverage derived from the data, not from the switch
Before: 11/11 nodes drawn today; 0 tests tie the drawn set to DAMAGE_PIPELINE
After: 1 derived test; a seeded extra node goes red
Method: simulation - read the switch; the seeded-red step needs a data mock, left for the wave
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
DamagePipelineFlow.tsx:244 default: return null;
DamagePipelineFlow.tsx:226 aria-label={`IncomingDamage pipeline flow diagram, ${DAMAGE_PIPELINE.length} steps`}
instrument: RTL test: every DAMAGE_PIPELINE id renders pipeline-node-<id>; seed with vi.mock of pipeline-data adding a node -> red

title: HitStopTimeDilation exists in C++ but no tuner knob or export reaches it
body:
## Summary
GA_MeleeAttack.h declares three combat-feel UPROPERTYs; the PoF tuner and its Python export drive only two, while the export header still names the third.

## Description
UE tree Source/PoF/AbilitySystem/GA_MeleeAttack.h:127,131,139 declares HitStopDuration, HitStopTimeDilation (0.1) and HitCameraShakeScale. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/polish/combat-feel-export.ts:5 names all three, but MAPPED covers only hit_stop_duration and hit_camera_shake_scale, and FEEDBACK_PARAMS (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/_shared/data.ts:157-164, combat-metrics-owned) has no time-dilation knob. Fixed: add a hitstopTimeDilation param (0-1) to FEEDBACK_PARAMS and map it; since caee1878 the export picks rows up from the table.

## Flow
- Combat > Feedback: no control for hitstop slow-down
- the exported script never sets hit_stop_time_dilation, so UE always uses 0.1

## Expected impact
Designers tune the hitstop slow-down from PoF like the other two knobs. Risk: a new FEEDBACK_PARAMS row changes preset matching unless FEEDBACK_PRESETS get the value.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every C++ feel property is reachable from the tuner
Before: 2 of 3 GA_MeleeAttack feel UPROPERTYs reachable
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - grepped the UE header; the knob belongs in combat-metrics' _shared/data.ts (out of scope)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
GA_MeleeAttack.h:131 float HitStopTimeDilation = 0.1f;
combat-feel-export.ts MAPPED = { hitstopDuration: 'hit_stop_duration', shakeScale: 'hit_camera_shake_scale' }
instrument: extend src/__tests__/lib/combat-feel-export.test.ts: the script sets hit_stop_time_dilation from a FEEDBACK_PARAMS row; red today; needs the combat-metrics owner
